chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba, from Ali ibn Abd al-'Aziz, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: "Shall I inform you of the root, branch, apex, and crest of Islam?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Its root is Salat (prayer), its branch is Zakat (alms-tax), and its apex and crest is Jihad (striving) in the path of Allah."
"Shall I inform you of the gates of goodness?"
"Fasting is a shield against the Fire."
ai.seo_question: What are the root, branch, and apex of Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) employs an agricultural metaphor to delineate the hierarchy of Islamic obligations, positioning prayer as the foundational root, zakat as the productive branch, and jihad as the fruiting apex. He further elucidates the spiritual utility of fasting, describing it not merely as a ritual but as a protective shield (junnah) against the fire, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegetical tradition regarding the purification of the soul.
